mainTopic: When טמא items of a שרץ join together to reach the שיעור for טומאה, the source that שרץ blood is טמא, and the start of the story of the Roman decrees.
overview: The amud opens with רבא's answer to רב אדא בר אהבה: the Torah links animals to שרצים only for the איסור of בל תשקצו, not for the שיעור needed for טומאה. A new משנה then teaches that the blood and meat of a שרץ join together (מצטרפין) to reach the size needed to make something טמא. רבי יהושע adds a rule: items join only if both their טומאה and their שיעור are the same. In the גמרא, רב זעירא limits the משנה to blood and meat from the same creature. A teaching of רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא seems to say all שרץ pieces join. רב יוסף answers that one source speaks of a whole creature and the other of only part of one. The גמרא proves this split from a ברייתא about blood spilled on a slope. Then רבי מתיא בן חרש asks רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in Rome for the source that שרץ blood is טמא, and this opens a story about Roman decrees against שבת, מילה, and נדה. רבי ראובן בן איסטרובלי gets the decrees canceled, but they return once he is found out, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Torah's comparison is only for the prohibition, not for sizes
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רב אדא בר אהבה: the Torah's הקש linking animals to שרצים teaches only the איסור of בל תשקצו. It does not teach anything about שיעורין of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When the Torah compares them, it is only for the prohibition of 'do not make yourselves disgusting.' But for measurements, it does not compare them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is answering a question from the previous discussion. The question was why animals are not given the same small size for טומאה as a שרץ, since the Torah mentions them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הקש (a comparison the Torah makes by placing two things side by side) can be limited to one area of law. רבא says this הקש teaches only that eating any of these things falls under the איסור of בל תשקצו. So the שיעור for a נבלה stays a כזית and does not shrink to a שרץ's כעדשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Comparing two things because the Torah places them together, so a law of one applies to the other
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as the One who gave the Torah
The prohibition against making oneself disgusting by eating repulsive things
The set amounts or sizes that make a law take effect

steps.whatToRemember: A הקש can apply to one area of law (the איסור) without applying to another area (the שיעור of טומאה).
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the animals and שרצים have nothing in common. He is saying the Torah's comparison works only for בל תשקצו and does not carry over to the size needed for טומאה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering רב אדא בר אהבה, who asked the question just before this.

phrases.english: When the Merciful One compares them,
it is for 'do not make yourselves disgusting,'
but for measurements, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי קָא מַקֵּישׁ רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge from the previous section of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the הקש to one law only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah compares animals to שרצים, maybe they should share the שרץ's small שיעור of כעדשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הקש teaches only the איסור of בל תשקצו. The שיעורין of טומאה are not affected.

steps.title: Blood and meat of a creeping creature combine
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that the blood of a שרץ and its meat join together to make up the size needed to make something טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The blood of a creeping creature and its meat join together with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the blood and the meat of a שרץ can be added together to reach the כעדשה size needed for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of a שרץ is itself טמא, the same way its meat is. So a small piece of meat plus a little blood can together reach the full שיעור, even if neither one reaches it alone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our משנה', the marker that a משנה text begins here
One of the eight small creeping creatures the Torah lists as טמא
Join together, so two smaller amounts count as one full amount
The size of a lentil, the שיעור for טומאת שרץ

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The blood of the creeping creature and the meat
join together with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ דַּם הַשֶּׁרֶץ וְהַבָּשָׂר מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: combining amounts for טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood and meat of a שרץ combine to reach the שיעור of טומאה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's rule for when items combine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע gives a general rule. Items combine only when both their type of טומאה and their שיעור are the same. If only one matches, or neither matches, they do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said a general rule: Anything whose impurity and whose measurement are the same joins together. If the impurity is the same but not the measurement, or the measurement is the same but not the impurity, or neither the impurity nor the measurement is the same, they do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע turns the specific case of the משנה into a general principle about when two different טמא items can be added together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two conditions must both be met: the same kind of טומאה (how strong it is and how long it lasts) and the same size requirement. For example, a שרץ and a נבלה both make a person טמא until evening, but their sizes differ (כעדשה versus כזית), so they do not combine. A מת and a נבלה share a כזית size, but their טומאה differs, so they do not combine either.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
Its impurity, meaning the type and strength of its טומאה
Equal or the same
They do not join together

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, two items combine only if BOTH their טומאה and their שיעור are the same. If either one differs, they do not combine.
steps.confusionAlert: It is not enough for the two items to share only the same size, or only the same type of טומאה. Both must match.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said a general rule:
Anything whose impurity and measurement are the same joins together.
Its impurity is the same but not its measurement,
its measurement is the same but not its impurity,
neither its impurity nor its measurement:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'nor', is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: they do not join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כֹּל שֶׁטּוּמְאָתוֹ וְשִׁיעוּרוֹ שָׁוִין מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the specific case of blood and meat into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items combine only when their טומאה and their שיעור are both the same.

steps.title: The גמרא begins with a statement from רב חנין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a statement that רב חנין reports in the name of רב זעירא. The printed text gives only the names. As the next steps show, רב זעירא held that the blood and meat of a שרץ join together only when they come from the same creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב חנין said in the name of רב זעירא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a statement from רב זעירא. Our printed text gives only the names, but the next steps show what he held: blood and meat of a שרץ join only when they come from the same creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זעירא narrows the משנה. Blood and meat combine only from one and the same שרץ, not blood of one creature with meat of another. Step 5 challenges this limit, and step 6 defends it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנִין אָמַר רַב זְעֵירָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chanin said that Rav Zeira said:
phrases.notes: His words aren't written out here. The next steps show he means blood and meat join only from the same שרץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנִין אָמַר רַב זְעֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה about blood and meat of a שרץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood and meat of a שרץ combine only when they come from the same creature.

steps.title: A ברייתא says all שרץ pieces join together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא brings a teaching from the word הַטְּמֵאִין: שרץ pieces join together, even meat with blood, and even from two different types of שרץ. This seems to go against רב זעירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא said: The word 'the impure ones' teaches that they join together. This is true even for a שרץ with another שרץ, and for a שרץ with blood, whether they are the same type or two different types!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to contradict רב זעירא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the plural word הַטְּמֵאִין, and from it this teaching learns that different pieces add up together. It says this works even for meat of one שרץ with blood of another, and even across two types of שרץ. That clashes with רב זעירא, who allowed joining only within the same creature.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The impure ones', the plural word in the פסוק that teaches joining together
They join together to make up the needed size
From one type / from two different types

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And similarly, Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina said:
phrases.notes: Even though this opens with 'and similarly', the next step's answer, 'it is not difficult', shows the גמרא treats it as a contradiction.

phrases.english: 'The impure ones' teaches that they join together,
and even a creeping creature with a creeping creature,
a creeping creature with blood,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִשֵּׁם אֶחָד, בֵּין מִשְּׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת!
phrases.english: whether from one type or from two types!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב זעירא's statement from step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says meat and blood of a שרץ join together in every case, which seems to contradict רב זעירא.

steps.title: Whole creature versus part of a creature
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says there is no contradiction. The ברייתא speaks of pieces from a whole שרץ, and רב זעירא speaks of pieces from part of a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not difficult. Here, it is talking about all of it. There, it is talking about part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by saying each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the meat and blood come from a whole creature, they join together, like the ברייתא says. When they come from only part of a creature, they do not join, like רב זעירא says. So both sources are right, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
All of it, the whole creature
Part of it

steps.whyThisMatters: This split between 'all of it' and 'part of it' is what the rest of the discussion tries to prove.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult.
Here, with all of it.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא: the meat and blood came from a whole שרץ.

phrases.english: There, with part of it.
phrases.notes: This is רב זעירא's case: the pieces came from only part of a שרץ.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רב זעירא seemed to argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a whole creature; רב זעירא is about part of a creature.

steps.title: Proof from blood spilled on a slope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for רב יוסף's split and brings a ברייתא: blood spilled on a slope makes a person טמא only if he overshadows all of it, not just part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where do we see this? From a ברייתא: If blood spilled on the floor and the spot was sloped, if a person overshadowed part of it, he is pure. If he overshadowed all of it, he is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that 'all of it' and 'part of it' can lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a slope, the blood runs and spreads out. The ברייתא says only covering all of it makes the person טמא, but covering part of it does not. This seems to show that 'all' versus 'part' makes a difference, like רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? A request for a source
A slope, a slanted surface
He overshadowed; he was over it like a tent, which can pass on טומאה

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?
From what was taught in a ברייתא:
It spilled on the floor
phrases.notes: This is talking about a רביעית of blood from a dead body.

phrases.english: and its spot was sloped,
if he overshadowed part of it, he is pure;
if he overshadowed all of it, he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב יוסף's answer in step 6
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's split between 'all of it' and 'part of it'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about blood spilled on a sloped floor

steps.title: What does 'part of it' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'part of it' means in the ברייתא. If it means part of the blood, that causes a problem with רבי's ruling that a stirred רביעית of blood is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'part of it' mean? If you say it means part of the blood, but didn't רבי חנינא say in the name of רבי: A רביעית of blood that someone stirred is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the words 'part of it' mean in the ברייתא it just brought, and tests the first possible meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'part of it' just means part of the blood, the ברייתא would imply that covering a full רביעית makes a person טמא. But רבי ruled that when a רביעית was stirred, the person stays pure, since the blood is no longer a full, joined-together רביעית. So the first reading runs into trouble, and the גמרא will need another meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a possible meaning that will be tested
A quarter-לוג of blood, the amount of blood from a dead body that makes things טמא
He stirred

phrases.english: What does 'part of it' mean?
If you say part of the blood,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Chanina say in the name of Rabbi:
A quarter-log of blood that he stirred is pure!
phrases.notes: Some of the blood sticks to the spoon, so it's no longer one full רביעית together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the proof ברייתא from step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'part of it' means in the ברייתא about the sloped floor
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'part of it' as part of the blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's ruling shows a stirred רביעית does not make a person טמא, which does not fit this reading.

steps.title: The proof works: whole versus part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא really is talking about a whole corpse versus part of a corpse, which supports רב יוסף's split.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it right to learn from here that one case is about a whole one and the other is about part of one? Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8 and closes the proof. 'Part of it' in the ברייתא is not part of the blood. It means blood that came from part of a body, as opposed to a whole body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 'part of it' as part of the blood ran into trouble with רבי's ruling. So the גמרא reads it as a difference between blood from a whole body and blood from part of a body. Since the ברייתא itself treats 'whole' and 'part' differently, רב יוסף's answer about a whole שרץ versus part of a שרץ is backed up.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that... (introduces the only reading left)
learn from it; we can conclude this

steps.whatToRemember: A whole שרץ is more significant than part of one. Pieces from a whole שרץ join together (the ברייתא), and pieces from part of a שרץ do not (רב זעירא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the contradiction from Step 5. רב זעירא and the ברייתא do not argue; they are talking about different cases.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it right to learn from this:
here, it is from a whole one,
phrases.notes: He means blood that came from one whole body.

phrases.english: there, it is from part of one?
Yes, learn it from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8 and completes the proof begun in Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא tells apart a whole body and part of a body, which supports רב יוסף's split between a whole שרץ and part of a שרץ.

steps.title: Where do we learn that שרץ blood is טמא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מתיא בן חרש asks רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, in Rome, for the source that the blood of שרצים is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מתיא בן חרש asked רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in the city of Rome: From where do we know that the blood of שרצים is טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins with a question. A sage asks for the Torah source that שרץ blood carries טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps already assumed that שרץ blood is טמא and joins with its meat. Now the גמרא looks for where in the Torah that rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: from where (do we know this)? A request for a source
the blood of creeping creatures
ritually impure

phrases.english: Rabbi Matya ben Charash asked

phrases.aramaic: אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי בָּעִיר רוֹמִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai in the city of Rome:
From where do we know that the blood of שרצים is impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the source for the טומאה of שרץ blood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that the blood of שרצים is טמא.

steps.title: The source is the פסוק 'וזה לכם הטמא'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers that the source is the פסוק 'וְזֶה לָכֶם הַטָּמֵא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because the פסוק says, 'And these are impure for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי gives the source. It comes from the words 'וְזֶה לָכֶם הַטָּמֵא' in the section about שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'הַטָּמֵא' are read as adding something beyond the body of the שרץ, and that something is its blood. This matches Step 5, where a lesson was also drawn from the word הטמאין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and these are impure for you', the words used as the source

phrases.english: He said to him: Because the verse says:
"And these are impure for you."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: וְזֶה לָכֶם הַטָּמֵא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word הַטָּמֵא in 'וְזֶה לָכֶם הַטָּמֵא' teaches that שרץ blood is טמא.

steps.title: The students praise him, but it was a known teaching
steps.stepSummary: The students are amazed at רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's wisdom. רבי מתיא answers that this was a set teaching of רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: How wise is בן יוחאי! He said to them: It is a set teaching in the mouth of רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The students are impressed by the answer. רבי מתיא tells them the teaching was not new; it was a fixed teaching that רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי already had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מתיא explains where רבי שמעון בן יוחאי got this teaching. That is why the story that follows is told: it explains how the two of them came to be together.

keyTerms.meaning: wise
a set, well-known teaching

phrases.english: His students said to him:
How wise is ben Yochai!
He said to them:
It is a set teaching in the mouth

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: חֲכֵים לֵיהּ בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the answer in Step 11 and gives its original source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The source for the טומאה of שרץ blood was a set teaching of רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The government's harsh decree
steps.stepSummary: The background story: the government once decreed that Jews may not keep שבת or give their sons a ברית מילה, and must be with their wives while they are נדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For once the government issued a decree that they may not keep שבת, they may not circumcise their sons, and they must be with their wives while they are נדות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story to explain the background of what רבי מתיא just said. This step sets the scene: a decree against three basic מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree targeted שבת, מילה, and the laws of נדה. The next steps tell how the Jews fought it, and that is how the sages came to be together.

keyTerms.meaning: the (non-Jewish) government
a decree
women in their time of נדה impurity

phrases.english: For once the government issued a decree
that they may not keep Shabbos,
and that they may not circumcise their sons,
and that they must be with their wives while they are נדות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the story that explains Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background: a decree against שבת, מילה, and the laws of נדה.

steps.title: A clever argument cancels the שבת decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי ראובן בן איסטרובלי disguises himself as a non-Jew and argues that letting Jews rest on שבת will make them poor. The officials agree and cancel that decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ראובן בן איסטרובלי went, cut his hair in a non-Jewish style, and sat with them. He asked: If a person has an enemy, should the enemy become poor or rich? They said: Poor. He said: Then let the Jews not work on שבת, so they become poor! They said: He spoke well. Let the decree be canceled. And they canceled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. A sage blends in with the officials and uses their own hatred of the Jews to get the שבת decree canceled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue that שבת is good. He argues that resting hurts the Jews by costing them a day of work. The officials accept this and cancel the שבת decree. The other decrees are still in place at this point.

an enemy
work (forbidden on שבת)
let it be canceled

steps.confusionAlert: Only the שבת decree is canceled here. The decrees on מילה and נדה are dealt with in the next two steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת decree was canceled through רבי ראובן בן איסטרובלי's clever argument.

steps.title: Canceling the decree against ברית מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ראובן בן איסטרובלי argues that ברית מילה weakens the Jews, so an enemy should let them do it. The officials agree and cancel the decree against מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He spoke to them again: 'If someone has an enemy, should the enemy be weak or healthy?' They said: 'Weak.' He said: 'If so, let the Jews circumcise their sons at eight days and become weak.' They said: 'He spoke well,' and they canceled that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: Still disguised, רבי ראובן בן איסטרובלי uses the same trick as with שבת, this time to cancel the decree against ברית מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he gets the officials to agree to a general rule: you want your enemy weak. Then he presents מילה as something that weakens the Jews. Since the officials think he is on their side, they accept the argument and cancel the decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method that canceled the שבת decree, now on the decree against מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decree against ברית מילה was canceled through רבי ראובן's argument.

steps.title: Canceling the decree about נדות
steps.stepSummary: Using the same method, he argues that keeping away from wives who are נדות means fewer Jews will be born. The officials cancel that decree too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He spoke to them again: 'If someone has an enemy, should the enemy grow in number or become fewer?' They said: 'Fewer.' 'If so, let them not be with women who are נדות.' They said: 'He spoke well,' and they canceled that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third decree. רבי ראובן gets the officials to cancel the rule forcing Jews to be with their wives while they are נדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, he first gets agreement on a general rule: you want your enemy to be few. Then he presents the הלכה of keeping away from נדות as something that makes the Jewish people smaller. All three decrees from step 13 have now been canceled.

keyTerms.meaning: Should increase or grow in number
Should become fewer
They will be with (their wives) as husband and wife
Women in the status of נדה, when a husband must keep away

steps.whatToRemember: With one clever method (agree that an enemy should be weak and few, then show the מצוה does exactly that), all three decrees were canceled: שבת, מילה, and נדה.

steps.title: He is found out and the decrees return
steps.stepSummary: The officials find out that רבי ראובן is Jewish, and they bring back all the decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: They recognized that he was a Jew, and they brought the decrees back.
steps.whatsHappening: The story takes a bad turn. The officials learn that their 'advisor' was Jewish, so they bring back all three decrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His arguments only worked because the officials thought he was one of them. Once they knew he was Jewish, they understood his arguments were meant to help the Jews, and they brought back what they had canceled.

keyTerms.meaning: They recognized him, they found out who he was
A Jew

steps.title: Who will go to cancel the decrees?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask who will go to Rome and get the decrees canceled. This sets up the next part of the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Who will go and cancel the decrees?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The Sages ask who will go to cancel the decrees, and the גמרא will answer this in the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is back and the trick cannot work again. This question leads into the story of who was sent to Rome. That is how רבי שמעון בן יוחאי ends up in Rome, where step 10 took place.
